newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico names bidders for $450 mln power plant.
newsitem.headline: Mexico names bidders for $450 mln power plant.

text.p: Three foreign bidders for a $450 million Mexican power plant project passed initial tender requirements on Tuesday, a spokesman for the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) said.
The three consortium passed technical prerequisites for the Monterrey II combined cycled power plant, Jose Luis Uribe Ortega told Reuters.
Bidders for the plant are: Japan's Mitsubishi Corp, Japan's Marubeni Corp and a union between Japan's Nissho-Iwai Corp and Swiss-Swedish ABB Energy Ventures Inc., the CFE said.
A decision on the winning bidder is due in the first two weeks of September, Uribe said.

Monterrey II is due to come on line in 2000 with electricity generating capacity of 450 megawatts, he said. The estimated construction cost is $450 million, Uribe added. The plant is part of a national spree of power plant tenders for the second half of the year. The new plants are aimed at boosting Mexico's output in anticipation of growing domestic electricity consumption.

In coming days a decision is also expected on the winning bid for the 100-megawatt Cerro Prieto IV power plant. Bids for the plant have come from Marubeni, Mitsubishi, Kanematsu-ICA Fluor Daniel, Ansaldo de Mexico and Ormet International-GEC Alsthom-Turalmex.
